modules.doc: Every Plugin has a data folder of its own, in the app's data folder (next to the State; never the config folder, never on the network), and `roster.storage` reads and writes files there by name (decision Q93). No permission: it's the Plugin's own, and nothing else is reachable through it. A name is a plain file name (letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`, not starting with `.`; at most 100 characters), never a path, so there's no way out of the folder; a link there (a symlink, or a junction on Windows) is never followed. A write replaces the whole file at once (a temporary file, then a rename), so a crash leaves the old file or the new one, never half of one. A file holds at most 1 MB, the folder 10 MB in at most 1,000 files. The folder goes when the Plugin is removed (`:plugins remove`, or `:packages clean` for a Package), and stays across reloads, updates and revoked permissions. The time the disk takes doesn't count against the Plugin's budget.
modules.name: roster.storage

modules.doc: `nil` unless the Plugin was granted `inventory.read` or `inventory.write`; each function is there only with its own permission. The reads but `request` wait for `roster serve`; that time doesn't count against the Plugin's budget, nor toward it being given up on. One call (a load, an event, an action, an answer) reads the Inventory once: `hosts()` and `groups()` in it share one answer of serve's, until a call into serve that can change something (a write, `mesh.cut`, …) in the same call. [`roster.inventory.request`](#rosterinventoryrequestdone) doesn't wait: prefer it where the Plugin would otherwise hold up the user, and for a big Inventory.

modules.doc: `nil` unless the Plugin was granted at least one `serve:<method>` permission. roster serve answers several requests at once, but a call can still wait: for its turn (2 calls into serve at a time for each Plugin, 4 for all of them) or behind the app's own write (a Publish: a minute or two). [`roster.serve.request`](#rosterserverequestmethod-params-done) doesn't wait: prefer it in anything the user starts. A job's progress comes as the `job_progress` event (serve API 20). [`roster.serve.call`](#rosterservecallmethod-params) waits, and the user's next action in the Plugin waits behind it; the wait never counts against the Plugin.
modules.name: roster.serve

modules.doc: `nil` unless the Plugin was granted at least one `network:<site>` permission ([Permissions](plugins.md#permissions)). The request runs in roster's core, never in the app's window, and doesn't wait: the function you pass gets the answer later, as a call of its own with a call's budget. Only the sites granted are reached, redirects included; a name that resolves to an address on this computer or a private network is refused unless the manifest lists the address itself, or the name as a private site (`network:private:nas.lan`), which reaches only private addresses. A pinned site (`#sha256:…`) trusts only that certificate. No cookies or credentials of roster's go along, and no proxy but the user's `plugin_proxy`, through which a public name is still looked up here first, refused if it leads inside, and reached only at the address roster checked (the proxy is asked for a tunnel to that address, never the name; a name this computer can't look up isn't sent). At most 4 requests at once, a 256 KB body out, a 1 MB body back, 30 seconds each.
